name: Persinger-Swann 1998: six circumcerebral configurations (CCW)
origin: Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook (Laurentian University), using the lab's standard circumcerebral protocol (Cook et al. 1999); given once to the former SRI remote viewer Ingo Swann during his 11-14 August 1998 lab visit
summary: The 30-min exposure that Persinger's lab gave Ingo Swann before his remote-viewing trials: six 5-min counter-clockwise rotations around the head, three with a burst-firing pattern and three with the frequency-modulated 'Thomas' pattern, using the point durations, gaps and per-coil step times of the paper's Table 1. Persinger et al. (2002) report that the fields altered Swann's experiences; this is one subject in one lab.
notes: Persinger et al. (2002) placed eight equally spaced solenoids in the horizontal plane 'between the midforehead and above the ears'; the ring Fpz, F7, T7, P7, Oz, P8, T8, F8 approximates it (the lab plane may sit slightly higher above the ears). The field steps counter-clockwise seen from above, one coil at a time with abrupt switching, in six configurations of 5 min (B1-B3 burst-firing, T1-T3 Thomas). Table 1 is mapped as follows: pixel duration = time per point; interstimulus time = silence after each pattern; commutator rate = dwell on the first coil; change in rate = added at each following coil of a rotation, which then starts again. Tsang et al. (2004) describe the same lab's change as applied to each of the other 7 solenoids but, like Persinger & Lavallee (2010), use '+' to mean shorter, which would give 20 to 6 ms and 200 to 214 ms here. The signs are read literally instead (+ longer, - shorter), giving 20 to 34 ms, 100 to 240 ms and 200 down to 186 ms per coil, because 100 ms minus 7 x 20 ms would be negative, Cook et al. (1999), the standard protocol the paper cites, report full turns of about 200 to 2000 ms (216 ms per turn here, 104 ms for 20 to 6 ms), and the Koren software patent (US 6,312,376) uses the plain sign. The schedule the lab actually ran was never published, so this mapping is an interpretation. Configuration 6's pixel duration is missing in the scan and is taken as 1 ms. The burst-firing and Thomas point files are not published, so built-ins stand in for them, keeping the published point counts: an accelerating burst of 230 points (Ryczko & Persinger 2002) sweeping 6 to 30 Hz at 3 ms per point (690 ms), and the built-in decelerating Thomas sweep, 25 to 6 Hz over 837 points (Dixon & Persinger 2001) at 3 ms per point (2511 ms). At 1 ms per point the same points play three times faster (230 ms at 18 to 90 Hz; 837 ms at 75 to 18 Hz), as a shorter pixel duration does with a fixed point file. The Lawson Cnp table (cnp generator; US 6,234,953, Persinger co-inventor) is another candidate for the Thomas pattern, but the research did not confirm it was the file used. The paper gives 2-5 uT, so the default is the low end, 2 uT; do not go above 5 uT. Persinger's lab reported that Swann felt 'floating in and out of his body' during configuration 4, and pressure in his ear with a marked suppression of his usual remote-viewing imagery during configuration 5. They also reported that his accuracy in trials on later days correlated with occipital 7 Hz spike-and-slow-wave activity. These are one subject, an unblinded exposure and post-hoc correlations, with no independent replication. Independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). The remote-viewing trials are left out of this file; run them blind with the app's photo-target trial guide, with a blinded sham session for comparison. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on headache, nausea or dissociation. Do not use results for decisions about real people, places or money.
setting: Blindfolded, in a comfortable chair in a quiet, dark room (Swann sat in an acoustic chamber and his reports were recorded by lapel microphone). Remote-viewing trials followed on later days: 4-6 hidden targets per session, about 2-3 min of drawing each, with EEG at F7, F8, T7, T8, O1 and O2.
schedule: One exposure in the original, with remote-viewing trials on the following days. For a self-test, randomise active and sham sessions blind and have the trials judged blind.
source: Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, Remote viewing with the artist Ingo Swann, Percept Mot Skills 94:927-949 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ (full text scan https://www.remoteviewed.com/biblo/papers/INGO%20SWANN%20NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL%20PROFILE-ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHIC%20CORRELATES-MAGNETIC%20RESONANCE%20IMAGING%20AND%20POSSIBLE%20MECHANISMS.pdf) ; Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Neurosci Lett 268:61 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2004, Int J Neurosci 114:1183 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15370182/ ; Ryczko & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 95:592 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12434855/ ; Dixon & Persinger 2001, Int J Neurosci 108:87 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11328704/ ; Tiller & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:26 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11883572/ ; CIA, SRI Studies in Remote Viewing: A Program Review https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/document/cia-rdp96-00787r000200090018-4 ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 ("20+2" notation) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Koren & Persinger, US 6,312,376 B1 (sequence interval and sequence acceleration) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6312376B1/en ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/

phases.name: B1 Burst-firing: 1 ms points, 1 ms gap, 20-34 ms per coil
B2 Burst-firing: 3 ms points, 1 ms gap, 100-240 ms per coil
B3 Burst-firing: 1 ms points, 3 s gap, 200-186 ms per coil
T1 Thomas: 1 ms points, 1 ms gap, 20-34 ms per coil
T2 Thomas: 3 ms points, 1 ms gap, 100-240 ms per coil
T3 Thomas: 1 ms points, 3 s gap, 200-186 ms per coil
